bullets.title: TSLA posts record revenue but margins collapse; stock nears worst earnings day ever
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 revenue hit a record $28B (+26% YoY, highest growth since Q2 2023) but net income fell 5% to $1.1B and operating margins cratered to 1.4% from 4.1% YoY. The stock was down 14.1% intraday—2nd worst earnings reaction in company history—with TSLA now -23% YTD vs. NDX +15%. Analysts noted management disclosed no metrics on unsupervised autonomous vehicles operating without safety operators, and Q2 deliveries of 480k (+25% YoY) did not offset the margin concerns. Elon's product roadmap extends meaningful revenue contribution to 2028, raising cash burn fears.

bullets.title: GOOGL: negative free cash flow for first time ever; 87% of record net income from equity markups
bullets.body: Google posted first-ever negative quarterly FCF of -$5.9B driven by massive AI capex, and raised full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B). Critically, 87% of the record $112B Q2 net income came from equity investment markups (SpaceX, Anthropic), with core operating net income only ~$33B, up just 2% QoQ. Google Cloud grew 81.8% YoY—fastest since separate reporting began—and Google Cloud CEO cited 50% YoY customer spend growth on CNBC. Piper Sandler cut PT to $395 (from $445) and Wells Fargo to $411 (from $418), both maintaining Overweight. Stock fell 7.6%, second-largest single-day earnings drop in company history.

bullets.title: AMD 'Advancing AI 2026': $1.4T accelerator TAM by 2030, CPU TAM expanding to $220B, Venice in full production
bullets.body: AMD CEO Lisa Su keynoted with major announcements: AI accelerator market forecast at $1.4T by 2030 (vs. entire semiconductor market today), overall compute market to reach $2T by 2030, and CPU TAM expanding from $60B to $220B driven by billions of AI agents requiring server cores. Venice EPYC is in full production with 20% performance lead over NVIDIA CPUs and wide lead over ARM chips; Venice-based systems ship Q4. AMD also announced a partnership with Cerebras combining Helios GPU racks with wafer-scale chips for ultra-low-latency inference launching H2 2026. New AMD chip features 320B transistors on TSMC 2nm/3nm. 2026 marks the first year inference compute exceeds training compute.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Groq as AMD partners Cerebras; CUDA moat erosion debate intensifies
bullets.body: One analyst framed the AI inference competitive dynamic as 'AMD partners with Cerebras, where NVIDIA buys Groq—fun times for premium inference.' Anthropic confirmed Claude can bootstrap on AMD Instinct + ROCm, with analysts arguing 'we are past the CUDA moat days.' Separately, OpenAI's infrastructure chief plans to work with AMD on MI500 series chips and is already using AMD Helios GPU racks. Intel and AMD also locked Chinese cloud firms into year-long CPU deals at prices up 40% amid export constraints.

bullets.title: Brent crude surges above $100/barrel on Iran/Houthi escalation; 10-year yield hits 4.70%
bullets.body: Brent crude rallied above $101/barrel (highest since June 3) as Iran kept Strait of Hormuz closed and Houthi attacks on tankers near the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal threatened Kazakhstan exports. Trump said he is 'seriously considering' a 'massive attack greater than anything before' on Iran. Simultaneously the US 10-year yield broke above 4.70% for the first time since January 2025 (above the 'Liberation Day' high), and Fed rate hike probability jumped from 12% to 36% in one week per CME FedWatch. 30-year mortgage rates hit 6.85%, the highest reading of 2026.

bullets.title: Mag 7 worst day since April 2025; broad selloff across equities, bonds, gold
bullets.body: The Magnificent 7 was on pace for its worst day since April 2025, with NASDAQ 100 down 2% and S&P 500 down 1.3% at open. One market observer noted 'the vast majority of asset classes are down—stocks, bonds, crypto, gold—with energy the sole notable exception.' CTA positioning flagged as amplifying the next leg lower given technical breakdown and oil headwinds. AAII bullish sentiment fell 15+ percentage points to 29.6%, the lowest since September, and SPX support cited at 7,480.

bullets.title: Google's $811B in contracted future capex commitments—up ~$500B in three months
bullets.body: Google disclosed $811B in contracted future spending commitments as of June 30, up nearly $500B from March 30, covering purchases under supply agreements and open purchase orders. Separately, $2.3T in broader AI financing commitments were highlighted as 'circular' and contingent on Anthropic/OpenAI monetizing $1.5T+ in unfunded obligations. Fitch noted US credit outlook is increasingly dependent on sustained AI investment confidence. One analyst argued declining hyperscaler FCF is weighing on bond markets and could drive forward rates higher.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike odds surge to 36% from 12%; ECB holds steady but warns energy inflation shock not yet fully felt
bullets.body: CME FedWatch implied probability of a rate hike jumped from 12% to 36% in one week. Separately, Fed officials appeared conflicted on July action—'I can make a good case for either raising rates or not'—with Iran reintroducing hawkish pressure after cooler inflation had reduced urgency. ECB held all rates steady (deposit at 2.25%) and Lagarde warned the 'full inflationary impact of the energy shock has not yet occurred,' flagging upside inflation risks and downside growth risks; energy expected to keep Eurozone CPI above target through H1 2027.

bullets.title: US initial jobless claims fall to lowest since 1969; KC Fed manufacturing misses
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims plunged to 187k (vs. 210k estimate and 209k prior), the lowest level since 1969. Continuing claims came in at 1.796M, below the 1.809M estimate. Separately, Kansas City Fed manufacturing index came in at 9 vs. 12 expected and 11 prior, with new orders falling to 10 from 13 and employment dropping sharply to 2 from 10—mixed macro signals.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure West US hit by intermittent connectivity failures and elevated latency since 14:44 UTC
bullets.body: Microsoft reported it is actively investigating networking and traffic-routing anomalies causing intermittent connectivity failures and elevated latency in the Azure West US region, with issues beginning at 14:44 UTC on July 23. Separately, Microsoft is testing a free ad-supported cloud gaming tier for Xbox Insiders.

bullets.title: GOOGL: token consumption slowdown on OpenRouter; users shifting to open-source models
bullets.body: One analyst flagged that token consumption growth slowed this quarter on OpenRouter and users are shifting toward open-source model downloads (e.g., Gemma), alongside reported supply capacity constraints, suggesting Google is losing AI momentum to competitors. Another analyst noted Google's photonics/networking capex allocation (40% of $44B) is driving strength in that sector even as the stock sells off.

bullets.title: NFLX: slowest revenue growth in over a year; analyst examines whether selloff creates opportunity
bullets.body: Netflix reported its slowest revenue growth in more than a year, triggering a stock selloff. At least one analyst is reviewing whether Wall Street is missing broader context and whether the pullback creates a buying opportunity, noting subscriber leadership and valuation as factors worth examining.

bullets.title: CMCSA: parks environment softening more than expected; NBCU split raises NFL rights strategy questions
bullets.body: Comcast flagged a softer-than-anticipated parks operating environment, with Orlando geography showing particular weakness even as Epic Universe performs well. The company also eliminated live earnings call Q&A and failed to clarify where FreeWheel/Universal Ads will be allocated in the planned NBC Universal split. One analyst raised the question of whether NBCU will prioritize locking in NFL rights beyond 2029 given the corporate separation timing.

bullets.title: AMD CPU TAM bear case: actual TAM came in well below BofA desk numbers per LYNX commentary
bullets.body: One account noted that AMD's CPU total addressable market figures presented at the event came in 'significantly below Bank of America desk numbers,' and that LYNX commentary on the day aligned with a bearish thesis on AMD. This contrasts with the bullish $220B TAM framing from AMD's own presentation, suggesting street expectations may have been higher.

bullets.title: Google's $94B SpaceX stake disclosed post-IPO; 87% of Q2 net income from equity markups
bullets.body: Google disclosed holding $94B in SpaceX shares following the SpaceX IPO. Combined with Anthropic and other stakes, these equity investment markups accounted for 87% of Google's record $112B Q2 net income—meaning core operational earnings were only ~$33B. This accounting dynamic is being flagged by multiple analysts as obscuring underlying business performance.

bullets.title: NVDA: RTX GPU prices rising again; cableless Blackwell design explained; DGX GB300 commissioned at Naval Postgraduate School
bullets.body: NVIDIA is passing increased memory kit costs to board partners, triggering another RTX GPU price hike. One tech observer noted Nvidia went cableless on Blackwell for reliability reasons after prior cable-related issues. Jensen Huang separately commissioned a DGX GB300 system at the Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey, providing AI computing access to 1,500 students and 600 faculty.

bullets.title: AAPL: Ford integrates Apple Maps into new EV platform; Apple sues OpenAI over post-smartphone era
bullets.body: Ford announced Apple Maps will be integrated directly into its upcoming Universal Electric Vehicle Platform and updated BlueCruise system. Separately, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, with observers framing it as a battle over who defines the post-smartphone computing era. Apple was also discussed on Odd Lots with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman exploring a potential AI comeback and possible CEO change.

bullets.title: MU options flow dominated by put sellers; $6M+ OTM AMD/SPY puts flagged as unusual
bullets.body: MU options flow was described as 'super active' with put selling dominating, typically a bullish/defensive signal. Separately, $6M+ in out-of-the-money puts on AMD and SPY were flagged as unusual activity, suggesting either large hedges or directional bearish bets at current levels.

bullets.title: NY AI data center moratorium; bipartisan AI 'kill switch' bill introduced
bullets.body: New York Governor Hochul defended her AI data center construction moratorium amid industry criticism. Separately, bipartisan House lawmakers (Obernolte R, Trahan D) introduced legislation that would allow the government to restrict deployment of AI models presenting catastrophic risks—an AI 'kill switch' bill—adding to the AI regulatory overhang.

bullets.title: RDDT: Needham bullish; third-party data adds positive signals; Google strategic dependency cited
bullets.body: Needham's Laura Martin was described as 'all bulled up' on Reddit, arguing Google has a strategic need for the platform. A third-party data shop in Ohio also added to positive intraday signals on RDDT, per a fintwit account tracking alternative data.
